from.place: Proof, opening sentence: 'Choose a compactification c=(j,p) of f'; replace this unjustified global choice over an unrestricted base by the Zariski-local extension of the same compactification formulas

title: Zariski-local extension of etale compact-support functors and exchange morphisms
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and use the bounded-below derived categories $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] for arbitrary schemes $T$ [def-pc-scheme]. For every separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], there are functors $H_h:D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\to D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, equipped simultaneously with the restriction comparisons, compactification comparisons, and exchange transformations specified below. Here $Ru_*$, $u^{-1}$, and $j_!$ mean the derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and degreewise extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], respectively; $L|_W$ denotes inverse image along an open inclusion. These data extend the compactification functors $Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] with their proper/open refinement maps [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].

For every $L\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and every open $V\subseteq B$, with $T_V=T\times_B V$ and $h_V:T_V\to V$, there are specified natural isomorphisms $(H_hL)|_V\cong H_{h_V}(L|_{T_V})$. For every compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $h$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper, there is a specified natural isomorphism $H_h\cong Rp_*j_!$. Write $r^h_{V,L}:(H_hL)|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{h_V}(L|_{T_V})$ for the restriction comparison. For $W\subseteq V\subseteq B$, it satisfies $r^h_{W,L}=r^{h_V}_{W,L|_{T_V}}\circ(r^h_{V,L}|_W)$, using the canonical identifications of iterated restrictions; $r^h_{B,L}$ is the identity. Write $q^h_c:H_h\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*j_!$ for the compactification comparison. For compactifications $c_i=(j_i:T\hookrightarrow\overline T_i,p_i:\overline T_i\to B)$ and a proper morphism $w:\overline T_1\to\overline T_2$ with $wj_1=j_2$ and $p_2w=p_1$, let $\alpha_w:j_{2!}\to Rw_*j_{1!}$ be [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Then $q^h_{c_1}=(Rp_{2,*}\alpha_w)\circ q^h_{c_2}$, inserting the canonical derived direct-image composition identification $Rp_{2,*}Rw_*\cong Rp_{1,*}$. Restricting $q^h_c$ to an open $V$ agrees with $q^{h_V}_{c|_V}\circ r^h_V$ under the open-restriction identification of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] for $p$ and the degreewise restriction of $j_!$. All these comparisons are natural in $L$. The functor $H_h$ takes complexes with cohomology in degrees at least $a$ to complexes with cohomology in degrees at least $a$, for every integer $a$.

For every Cartesian square with vertical maps $h:T\to B$, $h':T'\to B'$ and horizontal maps $v:T'\to T$, $u:B'\to B$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square], there is a specified natural transformation
$$e_{h,u,L}:u^{-1}H_hL\longrightarrow H_{h'}v^{-1}L.$$
It is natural in $L$ and commutes with open restrictions: for $V\subseteq B$ and $V'=u^{-1}V$, its restriction to $V'$ is $e_{h_V,u|_{V'},L|_{T_V}}$ under the preceding comparisons. If $h_V$ has a compactification $c_V$ and the pullback compactification $c'_V$ is used for $h'|_{V'}$, this restricted transformation is exactly the proper-exchange followed by extension-by-zero composite of [def-cbc-exchange-map], under the specified identifications with $Rp_{V,*}j_{V!}$ and $Rp'_{V,*}j'_{V!}$. The construction and this equality require no global compactification and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $B$ or $B'$.

source.place: Tags 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined) and 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek), section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification; agent formulation of the Zariski-local extension of their compactification functor and morphism constructions; the simultaneous existence and explicit compatibility data are an additional construction obligation. The tags themselves assume qcqs schemes, not the generality stated here.

proof.text: Fix $h:T\to B$. Use all affine open subschemes $U\subseteq B$ as a basis, not a cover whose intersections are assumed affine. The basis property is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $h_U:T_U\to U$ is separated and finite type. It is quasi-compact by the finite-type convention [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] first to $h_U$ and then to the identity of the affine scheme $U$ (whose diagonal and inverse images are identities): both $T_U$ and $U$ are qcqs. The nonempty cofiltered category $\operatorname{Comp}(h_U)$ of [prop-nagata-compactification-category] is therefore available. It includes all compactifications with quasi-compact open part, without imposing density; it is preserved by base change and has common and equalizing refinements. Form its small skeleton, and all subsequent parameter categories, in sufficiently large universes [def-weil-size-convention]. For the empty base the derived category is the zero category and the construction below is the unique zero functor.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, opening cofiltered-category argument, applied only over affine opens; agent affine-local setup

proof.text: Work before taking ordinary homotopy categories. Use [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] to identify the inverse image of the constant coefficient ring with the constant ring on the source. Apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to the constant inverse sequence $B_n=\underline\Lambda$ with identity transition maps on each small etale site, and take the constant cartesian section attached to a complex. Evaluation at the first level gives enhanced inverse image, its derived right adjoint, and open extension, together with the specified units, counits, pullback and direct-image compositors and their coherent mate constructions. These are the prescribed functors, not enhancements of arbitrary transformations of homotopy categories. The localization calculus [lem-coef-dg-derived-quillen-calculus] preserves strict enriched identity, composition and naturality diagrams and the mate formulas. In particular use the actual sheaf identifications of [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition]: every proper/open interchange is the same underlying section in the same support subsheaf. Their composition and pullback diagrams are identities of sheaf maps; applying the specified enhanced derived/mate constructions retains all their coherence homotopies. The resulting proper/open transformation is the one of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], since on an injective source and a resolution of its open extension its arrow is $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$. This also retains the vertical, horizontal and arbitrary-base-change equations stated there as coherent diagrams. We will use these specified coherences, rather than infer coherent diagrams from ordinary pointwise equalities.

source.place: Tags 0F7B, 0F7C, 0F7D, 0F7F, proper/open construction and strict underlying section maps; enhanced realization supplied by the cited generic tools

proof.text: For $c=(j_c,p_c)$ over an affine $U$, put $F_{U,c}=Rp_{c,*}j_{c!}$. For a refinement $w:c_1\to c_2$ use $Rp_{2,*}\alpha_w:F_{U,c_2}\to F_{U,c_1}$, with the derived direct-image compositor. The normalization of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] identifies this with exactly $\alpha_w$ from [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], not a freely chosen isomorphism. Its identity and vertical-composition assertions give the contravariant refinement diagram; step 2 supplies the higher coherences of that diagram. Every transition is an equivalence by its proper/open isomorphism assertion. Apply [lem-cbc-cofiltered-coherent-equivalence-diagrams] to $\operatorname{Comp}(h_U)^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the enhanced functor category. Take the homotopy colimit supplied by its filtered form and invert its equivalence structure maps. Obtain a functor $\Phi_{h,U}$ and an equivalence cone $q_{U,c}:\Phi_{h,U}\simeq F_{U,c}$ with all compatibilities. In particular $q_{U,c_1}=(Rp_{2,*}\alpha_w)q_{U,c_2}$. Cofilteredness and nonemptiness are from [prop-nagata-compactification-category]; the dual filtered form of the coherent-diagram lemma applies to the opposite category.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, cofiltered compactification argument with its proper/open normalization; enhanced cone is an additional agent construction

proof.text: For affine opens $V\subseteq U$, pull back a compactification $c$ over $U$ to $c|_V$ using [prop-nagata-compactification-category]. The canonical restriction map [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] and the open-extension comparison [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] identify $F_{U,c}(L|_{T_U})|_V$ with $F_{V,c|_V}(L|_{T_V})$. The base-change equation of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] makes these identifications compatible with every refinement $w$ and its pullback. For $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$, the two composites use the same iterated inverse image and the same mate for the pasted square, as supplied by the enhanced constructions in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; the open-extension pasting assertion supplies its corresponding factor. Thus these maps give coherent transformations of the refinement diagrams. The cone equivalence of [lem-cbc-cofiltered-coherent-equivalence-diagrams], including its naturality for indexing functors, produces coherent restriction equivalences $\Phi_{h,U}|_V\simeq\Phi_{h,V}$, with identity and iterated-restriction homotopies. This construction only uses affine inclusions. Any overlap of affine opens is handled by all affine opens contained in it, as guaranteed by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis].

source.place: Tag 0F7F, open-base-change specialization and restriction of compactifications; agent construction on the affine basis

proof.text: The local functors preserve each prescribed lower bound. Indeed $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so $\mathcal H^i(j_!L)=j_!\mathcal H^i(L)$ and the bound $a$ is unchanged. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose an injective representative of $j_!L$ with zero terms below that same $a$; enough injectives is provided by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The computation of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] represents $Rp_*j_!L$ by its termwise direct image, which again has zero terms below $a$. Hence $\Phi_{h,U}(L|_{T_U})$ has zero cohomology below the one bound $a$ of $L$, for every affine $U$. Restricting $L$ has this same bound by exactness of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. In particular the bound is uniform over the basis even when it is infinite.

source.place: Tag 0F7H, bounded-below compactification functor; explicit resolution verification of the unchanged lower bound

proof.text: For every $L$, steps 3 and 4 form a coherent cartesian affine-basis system $U\mapsto\Phi_{h,U}(L|_{T_U})$. Step 5 proves the common lower bound required by [lem-cbc-zariski-enhanced-derived-descent]. Apply its equivalence in the enhanced functor category with parameter $L\in\mathbf D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Define $\mathbf H_h$ by composing this system-valued functor with an inverse of that equivalence. This constructs its objects and arrows together. Pass to ordinary homotopy categories to obtain $H_h$ on $D^+$. Applying the same construction to $h_V$ for every open $V$ and using the open-restriction naturality of the descent equivalence gives $r^h_V:(H_hL)|_V\simeq H_{h_V}(L|_{T_V})$. Normalize the unit comparison to the identity. The coherent restriction diagrams become the exact identity and iterated-restriction equations in the statement. The lower-bound subcategory assertion of the descent lemma proves that $H_h$ preserves every bound $a$. Only the sites, bases and parameter categories in the fixed size convention are used; no global compactification is selected.

source.place: Agent globalization using enhanced bounded-below descent; Stacks Tag 0DA2 is the ordinary total-site descent prototype

proof.text: Suppose now $c=(j,p)$ is any global compactification of $h$. Its restriction to every affine $U$ is an object of $\operatorname{Comp}(h_U)$: properness of $p|_U$ is [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], openness of $j|_U$ is [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and quasi-compactness of $j|_U$ follows from the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The factorization identity pulls back. These arguments apply over arbitrary $B$; the qcqs-base compactification-category theorem is not applied to $B$. The restriction comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] and [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] identifies $(Rp_*j_!L)|_U$ with $F_{U,c|_U}(L|_{T_U})$. Thus the cone maps $q_{U,c|_U}$ of step 3 form a coherent equivalence of basis systems from the system defining $H_hL$ to that defining $Rp_*j_!L$. Use the mapping-complex/functor-category equivalence of [lem-cbc-zariski-enhanced-derived-descent] to obtain $q^h_c:H_h\simeq Rp_*j_!$. This is natural in $L$. For a global refinement $w:c_1\to c_2$, the base-change equation of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], applied as in step 4 to the open inclusion $U\subseteq B$ (where the module exchange map is the open-restriction isomorphism), identifies $(Rp_{2,*}\alpha_w)|_U$ with $Rp_{2,U,*}\alpha_{w|_U}$ under these restriction comparisons; so the restricted global refinement maps are the refinement maps of $\operatorname{Comp}(h_U)$. Performing this for the entire diagram of global compactifications simultaneously descends its cone equations, so for every global refinement $w:c_1\to c_2$ one gets $q^h_{c_1}=(Rp_{2,*}\alpha_w)q^h_{c_2}$ with the canonical compositor. Restriction of this same coherent cone to any open $V$ gives $q^{h_V}_{c|_V}r^h_V$, which is exactly the required compatibility of $q$ with $r$. These equations follow from coherent descent, not from a claimed faithfulness of ordinary derived restriction.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, comparison with a given compactification, extended by coherent Zariski descent

proof.text:
For a square $(h,u)$ take every affine $U\subseteq B$ and every affine $A\subseteq B'$ with $u(A)\subseteq U$. Such $A$ cover $B'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], since the inverse images of the affine opens $U$ cover $B'$. Over $U$ choose any $c\in\operatorname{Comp}(h_U)$ and pull it back to $A$. These compactifications and all their refinements exist by [prop-nagata-compactification-category]; the base-changed morphism remains separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Use the formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map] for the map
$$ (u|_A)^{-1}F_{U,c}(L|_{T_U})\longrightarrow F_{A,c_A}(v^{-1}L|_{T'_A}):$$
first the proper direct-image mate, then $Rp_{A,*}$ of the specified open-extension map. Step 2 makes this an enhanced transformation natural in $L$, via the actual mate and open-adjunction formulas, as [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] asserts. It is a map between bounded-below objects because inverse image is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and step 5 supplies the common bound for the target. No quasi-compactness of $u^{-1}U$ is used: its affine subopens $A$ are the test bases.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, displayed proper-exchange/open-extension composite, applied over affine pairs only

proof.text:
Check that these maps define one coherent transformation on the basis. Fix $w:c_1\to c_2$ over an affine $U$, write $w':c'_1\to c'_2$ for its pullback to $A$, and let $a_i:\overline T'_{i}\to\overline T_i$ be the projections. Put $\delta_w=Rp_{2,*}\alpha_w:F_{U,c_2}\to F_{U,c_1}$, and put $\delta_{w'}=Rp'_{2,*}\alpha_{w'}$. Let $E_i$ be the exchange composite of step 8 computed with $c_i$, and $\beta_i:a_i^{-1}j_{i!}\simeq j'_{i!}v^{-1}$ its open-extension factor. Apply the final equation of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] to the square with top $j_1$, bottom $j_2$, left vertical identity, right vertical $w$, and base change $a_2$. Its normalization identifies $\gamma$ with $\alpha_w$. Since exchange for the identity is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], the resulting equation is
$$ (Rw'_*\beta_1)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_w j_{1!})\circ(a_2^{-1}\alpha_w)=(\alpha_{w'}v^{-1})\circ\beta_2. $$
Insert the canonical direct-image compositors throughout. The composition-adjunction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{p_1}=(Rp'_{2,*}\operatorname{Ex}_w)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{p_2}Rw_*),\qquad p_1=p_2w.$$
Naturality of $\operatorname{Ex}_{p_2}$ for $\alpha_w$ therefore rewrites $E_1\circ(u^{-1}\delta_w)$ as
$$Rp'_{2,*}\big((Rw'_*\beta_1)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_w j_{1!})\circ(a_2^{-1}\alpha_w)\big)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{p_2}j_{2!}).$$
Substitution of the first displayed equation makes this
$$Rp'_{2,*}\big((\alpha_{w'}v^{-1})\circ\beta_2\big)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{p_2}j_{2!})=(\delta_{w'}v^{-1})\circ E_2.$$
This proves the exact refinement equation $E_1\circ u^{-1}\delta_w=(\delta_{w'}v^{-1})\circ E_2$, with every factor in the prescribed direction. These are the coherent diagrams of step 2, so [lem-cbc-cofiltered-coherent-equivalence-diagrams] descends them to the $\Phi$ cones. For a smaller affine $A_0\subseteq A$ and $U_0\subseteq U$ through which its map factors, the enhanced proper mate pasting and the open-extension pasting comparison give the same formula after restriction [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. If two affine opens $U_1,U_2$ can be used, cover $A\cap u^{-1}(U_1\cap U_2)$ by affine $A_0$ mapping into affine $U_0\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$. The previous comparison handles both choices there, and the coherent basis-descent equivalence [lem-cbc-zariski-enhanced-derived-descent] identifies the two transformations with their specified overlap homotopies. Higher overlaps use the same diagram for strings of inclusions and refinements, already retained in step 2; thus the argument constructs coherent matching maps rather than merely matching ordinary derived components.

source.place: Tags 0F7F and 0F7L, compactification-independence and open restriction; mate pasting spells out the compatibility needed for descent

proof.text: Use [lem-cbc-zariski-enhanced-derived-descent] on $B'$ with the parameters $L$ and the coherent transformation just constructed. Under its functor-category equivalence the source basis system is the restriction of $u^{-1}H_hL$, using the restriction cones of step 6, and the target is that of $H_{h'}v^{-1}L$. The descended arrow is $e_{h,u,L}$. Its naturality in $L$ and its compatibility with restriction to $V'=u^{-1}V$ are the descended naturality and restriction diagrams from steps 8 and 9. If $h_V$ has a specified compactification $c_V$, repeat step 7 on $V$ and on its pullback $V'$ using those compactifications. The definition in step 8 is then, as a coherent diagram of functors on the affine bases, exactly the proper-exchange/open-extension formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map]; the descent equivalence identifies that coherent diagram with the global formula on $V'$. This proves equality with the required specified map, including when $V$ or $V'$ is not qcqs. It supplies all the asserted data simultaneously. The only compactification existence invoked was over affine opens, while all globalization used the stated arbitrary-basis descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, exchange normalization; agent descent of the simultaneously constructed transformation

proof_origin.place: Tags 0F7I and 0F7L give the qcqs compactification formulas; the arbitrary-base globalization is an agent construction using explicit enhanced coherent descent tools.
